en: The Thirteen-Book Collection of Birth Stories,
Chapter on Mangoes (Ambavagga)
5. The Dūta Jātaka “O Brahmā,
while you were meditating on the bank of the Ganges, I sent a messenger to you.”
When questioned about them, he did not explain;
was suffering a secret doctrine to you?
"If suffering were to arise for you..."
O increaser of the kingdom of Kāsi,
do not tell him of this [teaching] to one who will not liberate you from suffering.
Whoever, by means of the Dhamma, should liberate even a single part of that person who has come to suffering;
One may indeed declare it to him:
the cries of jackals and the calls of birds are easy to understand.
The scent of human urine, O King,
is even more difficult to discern than that;
yet a person might still think:
Whether called kinsman, friend,
or companion— he who was formerly well-disposed but later becomes otherwise.
When a person, being questioned about their own suffering,
reveals it at an improper time,
their friends become joyful.
Those who wish him well become sorrowful for him.
But when they know that such a person has reached his time,
and have perceived the single-mindedness of those wise ones;
A wise person, though knowing the harsh words of another,
should utter speech that is gentle and meaningful;
and if he should know it to be beyond his own power, [he should remain silent].
For they do not lead to my happiness;
rather, the wise man alone, looking toward truth, integrity, and moral dread, should endure these intense sufferings.
Wandering through the kingdom,
through market towns and royal capitals,
begging for alms, O Great King.
Desiring wealth for his teacher,
he approached householders, royal officers,
wealthy merchants, and brahmins.
I obtained seven coins of gold, O lord of people;
those were lost to me, O Great King.
Therefore, O Great King, I grieve greatly for those men who have merely reflected upon this in their minds.
They are not able to liberate one from suffering;
therefore, I did not speak with them.
But you, O Great King, are indeed [able to do so] for me.
"Having reflected upon this with my mind,
it is sufficient to liberate one from suffering;
therefore, I have declared it to you."
“Out of faith in him,
the prosperer of the kingdom of Kāsi,
gave a deposit in a golden casket.”
"Of gold, there are fourteen.
Thus ends the fifth Jātaka, the Dūta-jātaka.
